reviewMethod: Specification page images and text reviewed at the saved source hash; source-checked task analyses used to judge each operation, with explicit no-separate-skill decisions and alternative-route distinctions.
scope: Separate qualification-wide inventory of 35 skills and explicit skill-demand review of all 51 leaves in Physics Summer 2024 1P. A mapped skill is not an official task-AO allocation, complete teaching coverage or a validated template.
identifierPolicy: Experimental IDs use local one-based bullet ordinals, not publisher-assigned numbers. Mathematical IDs retain the printed category number and row letter. All IDs are local versioned references.

excludedMathematicalRows.reason: Sampling row has no Physics applicability tick.
Mode/median row has no Physics applicability tick.

skills.summary: Solve problems within practical situations.
Apply physical knowledge in practical contexts.
Plan investigations and choose techniques using scientific understanding.
Describe appropriate investigative methods, including safe and skilful techniques.
Observe and measure with suitable precision, recording and presenting results systematically.
Identify independent, dependent and control variables.
Interpret experimental data and draw conclusions supported by evidence.
Communicate experimental findings using technical language, calculations and graphs.
Assess experimental reliability.
Evaluate data and methods for factors affecting accuracy and validity.
Use decimal numbers.
Use standard-form numbers.
Use ratios, fractions, percentages, powers and roots.
Estimate simple calculations without a calculator.
Use sine and inverse sine with degree angles.
Choose suitable significant figures.
Calculate and interpret an arithmetic mean.
Construct and interpret bar charts.
Construct and interpret frequency tables, diagrams and histograms.
Use simple probability.
Use scatter plots to recognise relationships between two variables.
Calculate orders of magnitude.
Use inequality, proportionality and approximation symbols.
Rearrange equations.
Substitute values with appropriate physical units into equations.
Solve simple algebraic equations.
Translate between graphs and numerical information.
Recognise the linear relation y = mx + c.
Plot two variables from experimental or other data.
Determine linear-graph gradient and intercept.
Draw and use a tangent gradient as a rate of change.
Interpret area between a curve and the horizontal axis, including square-counting measurement.
Use angles measured in degrees.
Visualise two- and three-dimensional objects and their representations.
Calculate triangle and rectangle areas and cube surface areas and volumes.
